L01.note: -36 is the geometric middle of -9 and -144 (x4 each way), so it is the value the other two are built around.

L02.note: two reciprocal pairs (11/3,3/11 and 11/4,4/11) with nothing to separate them.

L03.note: 3 is the hub: -3 is its negation, 6 and 9 are its multiples.

L04.note: 5 = -((-2)+(-3)), i.e. built from the two negative options; 14 is the odd magnitude.

L05.note: no signal beyond -13/-10 being a near pair.

L06.note: 53/9 is the only non-integer and the only value not a multiple of 5; 45 and 15 are 5 scaled.

L07.note: all four are -2^k, a closed geometric set with no distinguished member.

L08.note: 3/-3 is a sign trap and 7 is the odd magnitude, but nothing picks a member.

L09.note: 128 = 4 x 32, the only value derivable from two others; 36 is the decoy magnitude.

L10.note: 6 and 36 form a square trap, leaving the 24/5, 24/7 fraction pair undecided.

L11.note: 0 is a weak key and 10 is off-magnitude, but -3 vs -2 is a coin flip.

L13.note: 12 = 3 + 9, the only value that is a sum of two others in the multiples-of-3 set.

L14.note: -19.5 is the only non-integer, so it reads as the computed value against three round decoys.

L15.note: 27/3 cube pairing and 18/2 pairing cancel out; no discriminator.

L16.note: -9/5 is assembled from parts appearing in the other options (9 and the 5 of 5/6), the classic composite key.

L17.note: structure is {3,13} and {4,14}, two parallel off-by-one pairs with no tiebreak.

L18.note: 16 = 2 x 8 is the derivational hub; 8/-8 is a sign trap.

L19.note: 403 is the non-round near-neighbour of the round decoy 400, the usual shape of a computed answer.

L20.note: four decimals with no arithmetic relation I can see.

L21.note: 1,2,3,4 is a count-type option set carrying no information.

L22.note: 9 (=27/3) is the round trap inside a thirds set; 29/3 is the adjacent ugly value such traps are built from.

L23.note: 26/3 anchors the set: -26/3 is its negation and the other two are smaller thirds.

L24.note: 11 is off-magnitude; the remaining -1/-2/4 give nothing.

L25.note: 16/18/21 cluster with -4 as the sign decoy; no pick inside the cluster.

L27.note: three ugly quarters/integers; -5/2 looks like the simple trap but -59/4 vs -209/4 is a coin flip.

L28.note: 14 and 21 share a factor of 7, which distinguishes the pair but not a member.

L31.note: reciprocal and same-numerator pairs cancel; no signal.

L32.note: 1/-1 sign pair plus two unrelated magnitudes; no signal.
